title: 'No Zalameda Court': Chief Justice vows to uphold judicial integrity
summary: Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda vowed on Monday to uphold integrity and independence in the judiciary as he began his tenure as the new head of the Supreme Court (SC).

blocks.text: Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda vowed on Monday to uphold integrity and independence in the judiciary as he began his tenure as the new head of the Supreme Court (SC).
Speaking at his first flag-raising ceremony, Zalameda stressed that under his leadership, there would be no “Zalameda Court,” but only a judiciary that answers to the people.
“To my colleagues, I am here to work with and for the Court. The way I see it, I am simply its humble representative,” Zalameda said.
“There is no Zalameda Court. There is only the Supreme Court of the Philippines, comprising us all, answering only to the people,” he added.
He said the occasion was meaningful as it gave him his first opportunity to address SC personnel in his capacity as Chief Justice.

“Gusto ko pong magpasalamat sa inyong pagtanggap sa akin (I would like to thank you for welcoming me). Let us carry forward our shared commitment to integrity and service in everything we do,” Zalameda said.
Zalameda said he accepted the responsibility entrusted to him with “humility, independence, and determination,” pledging to serve as a “servant of justice” until his last day in office.

Recalling the killing of Basilan Judge Joseph Wee Sit, Zalameda said the tragedy underscored the dangers faced by judges and court personnel but stressed that threats would not deter the judiciary from fulfilling its mandate.

“This tragedy is a sobering reminder of the very real dangers facing our judges and court personnel. Nakakalungkot po talaga (It's truly saddening). But stronger than our grief and outrage is our shared resolve. No threats will ever shutter our courts or silence the pursuit of justice,” he said.
He assured judges and court personnel that the SC would prioritize their safety and protect their independence.
“To our judges and court personnel, hindi kayo pababayaan ng Korte Suprema. Gagawin namin ang lahat upang matiyak ang inyong kaligtasan at mapangalagaan ang inyong kalayaan,” Zalameda said.
(To our judges and court personnel, the Supreme Court will not abandon you. We will do everything to ensure your safety and protect your independence.)
He also called on members of the justice sector to unite in protecting the judiciary's ability to deliver justice.
Zalameda took his oath on Nov. 6 as the Philippines' 28th Chief Justice, succeeding retired Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo.— MCG, GMA News
